definitions.explanation: A craftsperson who builds and repairs wooden structures and objects, especially houses and buildings.

examples.japanese: {大工|だいく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{修理|しゅうり}→修理：03214_shuuri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{頼|たの}んだ→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I asked a carpenter to repair the house.
My grandfather was a skilled carpenter.
examples.notes: 腕のいい = skilled, good at one's craft

examples.japanese: {大工|だいく}⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{体力|たいりょく}→体力：05318_tairyoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日曜|にちよう}{大工|だいく}→日曜大工：07078_nichiyoudaiku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{棚|たな}→棚：01650_tana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: My father built a shelf as a DIY project.
examples.notes: 日曜大工 = Sunday carpenter, DIY

examples.japanese: ⟦{宮|みや}→宮：noentry⟧{大工|だいく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{釘|くぎ}→釘：03881_kugi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}わずに→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦や→や：10080_ya⟧⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てる→建てる：01189_tateru⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っている→持つ：00478_motsu⟧。
examples.english: Shrine carpenters have the technique of building shrines and temples without using nails.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: Traditional Japanese {大工|だいく} (carpenters) are highly skilled craftsmen. The construction of traditional Japanese wooden buildings, including temples and shrines, requires specialized techniques passed down through generations.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧{大工|だいく} (town carpenter)
- ⟦{宮|みや}→宮：noentry⟧{大工|だいく} (shrine/temple carpenter - specialized)
- {大工|だいく}⟦{道具|どうぐ}→道具：01479_dougu⟧ (carpentry tools)
- ⟦{日曜|にちよう}{大工|だいく}→日曜大工：07078_nichiyoudaiku⟧ (Sunday carpenter, DIY enthusiast)

IDIOM: {大工|だいく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{掘|ほ}っ{立|た}て→掘っ立て：noentry⟧⟦{小屋|ごや}→小屋：02768_koya⟧ = 'The cobbler's children have no shoes' (lit. 'a carpenter's hastily-built shack')
